notes:
CIRCUIT: five inverting op-amp stages (integrator/differentiator style) drawn on one sheet. A 5V source drives stage A (U3, 1uF feedback), whose output feeds R5 into stage B (U2, 1uH feedback). A 10A current source drives stage D (U15, 1uH feedback); U15's output is the central distribution node that feeds R12 -> stage C (U10, 1uF feedback), C20 -> stage E (U19, 1uH feedback), and also the non-inverting input of U2. The three output resistors R4, R11, R21 tie together on a floating right-hand rail.

NET MAP (names as emitted by finalize):
  0   = ground: in+ of U3/U10/U15/U19, V-DC 6 bottom, I-DC 17 bottom, GND 7/8/14/18/22/23.
  n1  = output of U3 (x~330..378, y~197): U3.out, right lead of feedback cap C0, left end of R5. Site S7 dot.
  n2  = inverting input node of U3 (y~168 rail, x~120..220): U3.in-, left lead of C0 (via the x~185 riser), top of the 5V source.
  n3  = inverting input node of U2 (x~606, y~190): U2.in-, left lead of feedback inductor L1 (via the x~606 riser), right end of R5. Site S6 dot.
  n4  = output of U2 (x~755..809, y~206): U2.out, right lead of L1, left end of R4. Site S9 dot.
  n5  = CENTRAL NODE - output of U15. Members: U15.out (via the x~342 riser, site S21), right lead of L13, left end of R12, left lead of C20 (bottom of the x~442 column), and U2.in+ (top of the x~442 column, across the y~247 run). Site S19 dot.
  n6  = floating right-hand rail x~995, y 206..820: right ends of R4, R11 and R21. Site S17 dot. Nothing else touches it - this is what the drafter drew (three stage outputs bussed together with no load or reference).
  n7  = inverting input node of U10 (x~609, y~505): U10.in-, left lead of feedback cap C9, right end of R12. Site S16 dot.
  n8  = output of U10 (x~764..792, y~510): U10.out, right lead of C9, left end of R11. Site S18 dot.
  n9  = inverting input node of U15 (y~644 run, x~61..183): U15.in-, left lead of L13 (via the x~163 riser, site S27), top of the 10A current source.
  n10 = inverting input node of U19 (x~612, y~802): U19.in-, left lead of L16 (via the x~612 riser, site S37), right lead of C20.
  n11 = output of U19 (x~785..813, y~818): U19.out, right lead of L16, left end of R21. Site S38 dot.

SITE DECISIONS (all CRITICAL sites explicitly recorded; every one is a junction):
  S6 (606,190), S7 (379,196), S9 (809,206), S16 (609,505), S17 (988,508), S18 (792,510), S21 (342,565), S38 (813,817): each is a 3-branch tee carrying a clearly drawn solder blob (dot score 2.2-3.0); the blob is ~3x stroke width in both axes. Junction. Reading them as anything else would strand a feedback element (L or C) on a one-terminal net, which is impossible.
  S19 (442,524) deg=4, dot=3.2, hop=7.7: this is the only real judgement call. inkmap at (442,524) shows a symmetric filled blob spanning x 437..451 and y 518..531 - ~13 px in BOTH axes against a 3-4 px stroke - i.e. an unambiguous solder dot, not a corner or a stroke overlap. The reported hop=7.7 is a false positive picked up from the leftmost zigzag peak of R12, which sits ~30 px to the right, not from any semicircular hop at the crossing itself. Chosen: junction, so the U15 output, R12, C20 and U2.in+ are one node (n5). The alternative (crossing) would split it into (a) horizontal: U15.out + R12 and (b) vertical: U2.in+ + C20 left - which would leave C20/stage E driven only from the high-impedance non-inverting input of U2, i.e. a branch with no source, and would leave U2.in+ with no DC path anywhere. That reading is electrically nonsense, so the ink evidence and the electrical argument agree.
  S27 (163,644) and S37 (612,802) deg=3, no dot: inkmap shows a vertical stroke arriving from above and terminating on the horizontal run (a T, with only a 2-3 px pen overshoot below). One wire ending on another is a junction by definition. Reading them as crossings would leave the feedback inductor L13 / L16 with a dangling left lead.
  Non-critical sites S0-S4, S11-S13, S22-S26, S31-S36 are all handwritten value-label ink ('1uF', '1uH', '1kOhm', '10A', '5V') brushing a component box or a wire; left at the tracer default, they do not change the netlist.

PORT / PIN FIXES:
  Terminal-on-label errors (each produced a one-terminal net in the tracer output):
   - C0.t1 was on a stroke of the '1uF' text at (298,91) -> moved to p2, the real left lead at (243,67), which risers down to the U3 inverting-input rail (n2).
   - C9.t1 was on the '1uF' text at (711,423) -> moved to p1, the real right lead at (728,391), which risers down to the U10 output (n8).
   - I17.t1 was on the '10A' text at (105,758) -> moved to p2, the real bottom lead at (62,801), which goes to GND22 (net 0).
   - U15.t1 was on the '1uH' label above the box at (273,599) -> moved to p1 (183,642), the actual inverting-input lead.
   - U19.t1 was on the '1uH' label above the box at (737,754) -> moved to p1 (640,802), the actual inverting-input lead.
  Op-amp pin order (must be in+, in-, out; every one of the five was wrong in the tracer output, which simply used discovery order):
   - U2:  in+ = p0 (638,240) lower-left, next to the drawn '+'; in- = p2 (638,188) upper-left, next to the drawn '-'; out = p1 (763,206).
   - U3:  in+ = p2 (220,217); in- = p0 (220,175); out = p1 (329,198).
   - U10: in+ = p2 (634,552); in- = p1 (635,506); out = p0 (764,515).
   - U15: in+ = p4 (183,692) - a port the tracer had left unused, it runs down to GND18; in- = p1 (183,642); out = p0 (301,657).
   - U19: in+ = p5 (641,853) - likewise unused, runs down to GND23; in- = p1 (640,802); out = p0 (785,820).
  In all five the '+' is drawn on the lower input and the '-' on the upper input, legible in the _comps crops, so no physical-reading fallback was needed.

CLASSES: every symbol matches its label. Five Op-Amps, three Inductors (1uH), three Capacitors (1uF), five Resistors (1kOhm), one V-DC (5V), one I-DC (10A), six GND. No re-classification.

UNRESOLVED / CAVEATS: none blocking. The only oddity in the finished netlist is n6, the right-hand rail, which touches three resistor terminals and nothing else - no ground, no load. That is exactly what is on the paper (the x~995 column runs from R4's right end down to R21's right end with R11 tapping it at S17), so it is recorded as drawn rather than 'fixed'.
